bultum: life, lifetime (Harper bultu): bultišu (bu-ul-ti-šu) “his life, his lifetime”, in ina bultišu “in his lifetime”; the vowel and the sign TI are as Harper prints them, the noun itself is not otherwise met in these parts
wardūtum: slavery, the status of a slave (from wardum “slave” + the abstract ending -ūtum): wardūtim (wa-ar-du-tim, genitive) “of slavery”, in ana wardūtim “for slavery, as slaves”
nudunnûm: the marriage-gift, what the husband gives his wife (Harper nudunnū): nudunnam (nu-du-na-am, nu-du-un-na-am, accusative) “the marriage-gift”; the final vowel of the base is UNCERTAIN, the accusative -am is plain; distinct from the šeriqtum, the dowry from the bride’s father
zaḫāmum-D: UNCERTAIN: D-stem, to scheme, plot against (Harper “to scheme”; the root is not met elsewhere in these parts, so the sense rests on Harper and on the context): uzaḫḫamūši (u-za-aḫ-ḫa-mu-ši) “they scheme against her” (present, 3rd plural, with -ši “her”; the doubled ḫḫ is the D-stem)
emēdum: to lay on, impose; with arnam, arnam emēdum “to lay guilt (on oneself)”, i.e. to be in the wrong (Harper emēdu I,1): immidū (i-im-mi-du) “they have laid (guilt), they are in the wrong” (preterite, 3rd plural; the -u is the plural ending, the doubled m is the assimilated d of the root, spelled out in the sign mi); the whole sense of the clause, “the sons are in the wrong”, rests on this reading and is UNCERTAIN in its grammar
emēdum-N: N-stem of emēdum, to be joined, be attached (Harper emēdu IV,1): innemdū (in-ne-im-du) “they were joined, they have joined (as a couple)”, preterite 3rd plural; ištu innemdū “since they were joined”, said of a man and wife; the sense “joined” is from the N-stem’s passive use and the context
warkûm: later, subsequent (adjective, related to warka “afterwards”): warkîm (wa-ar-ki-im, genitive masculine) “later”, of the husband, ana mutiša warkîm “to her later husband”; warkūtum (wa-ar-ku-tum, plural in -ūtum) “the later ones”, said of children; the opposite of maḫrûm “first, former” and of panûm “former”
gadum: together with, along with (preposition; Harper gadu): gadum (ga-du-um) šeriqtim “together with the dowry”; takes the genitive
almattum: widow (Harper almattu); written with the Sumerian signs NU.MU.SU and not spelled out, the ending is read from the context: almattum “a widow” (nominative, as subject of the law), almattim “of the widow” (genitive); in the sense “woman whose husband has died”
panûm: former, earlier, previous (adjective, from pānum “front”): panîm (pa-ni-im, genitive masculine) “former”, said of a husband, mutiša panîm “her former husband”; set against warkûm “later”
unūtum: household goods, furnishings, gear (Harper unūtu): unīātim (u-ni-a-tim, plural oblique) “the household goods”; unūt (u-nu-ut) “household goods of” (construct state, before the genitive)

__broaden__.ḫīrtum: wife (Harper ḫīrtu): ḫīrtašu “his wife” · the free wife as against the slave-woman (amtum): ḫīrtim (ḫi-ir-tim, genitive) in mārī ḫīrtim “the sons of the wife”, ḫīrtum (ḫi-ir-tum, nominative) “the wife” as subject
__broaden__.warkatum: the circumstances, the facts of the case: warkassu “his case” (warkat + šu, t+š → ss) · UNCERTAIN: warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her case” (what is examined and decided) and “her estate” (what she leaves behind), the second reading resting on the context · the estate, the property left behind: warkat (wa-ar-ka-at, construct) bīt mutiša “the estate of her husband’s house”; warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her estate” in the clause adi balṭat ikkal … warkassa ša mārīšama “her estate is her sons’ alone” (UNCERTAIN where the clause fits both senses)
__broaden__.aplum: heir, son as heir (Harper aplu; spelled ab-lim, the sign read ab or ap): aplim “of an heir”, in kīma aplim ištēn “like one heir” · also written with the signs DUMU.UŠ (Harper TUR.UŠ, ablu), unspelled: aplum “the heir”, the son who inherits; the Sumerian writing can also mean “eldest son”, the choice rests on the clause (UNCERTAIN)
__broaden__.akālum: to eat; infinitive akālum “eating, food”: akālim “of eating”, in ša akālim ibašši “there is food” (literally “something of eating”) · with a possession as object or alone, “to have the use of” (a house, an estate), literally “to eat it”: ikkal (i-ik-ka-al, present) in adi balṭat ikkal “as long as she lives she shall eat (have the use of it)”; the sense “have the use of” is UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.erēbum: to enter: iterub “she has entered” (perfect; Harper I,2) · irrubu (i-ir-ru-bu) “she enters” and īrubu (i-ru-bu) “she entered” — present and preterite with the subjunctive -u, after lāma “before” and ištu “after” · irrub (i-ir-ru-ub) “she shall enter” (present, 3rd feminine); irrubu (i-ir-ru-bu) after inūma “when”; īrubma (i-ru-ub-ma) “she entered, and”, īrubu “(where) she entered”; erēbim (e-ri-bi-im) “of entering”, the infinitive in the genitive, in ana bītim šanîm erēbim “to enter another house”
__broaden__.rabûm-D: D-stem of rabûm: to bring up, raise: urabbāšu “she shall raise him” · urabba (present) “he shall raise (the orchard)” · urabbû (u-ra-ab-bu-u) “they shall bring up” (present plural), with young children as object
__broaden__.ezēbum-Š: UNCERTAIN: Š-stem of ezēbum “to leave”: to have left, have deposited (a document): uštēzib (uš-te-zi-ib, perfect, 3rd person); the Š-stem šūzubum elsewhere means “to save, rescue”, so the sense with a tablet (ṭuppam uštēzib) rests on the context · ušezzibūšunūti (u-še-iz-zi-bu-šu-nu-ti) “they shall make them leave (a tablet)” (present, 3rd plural, with -šunūti “them”), in ṭuppam … “they shall have them leave a tablet”; UNCERTAIN as before in its sense
__broaden__.ṣeḫrum: young; the child: mār awīlim ṣeḫram “the young son of a free man” · plural ṣiḫḫirū (ṣi-iḫ-ḫi-ru) “(who are) small”, said of children, and ṣiḫḫirūtim (ṣi-iḫ-ḫi-ru-tim) “the small ones”; UNCERTAIN whether the first is a stative or the plural of the adjective
__broaden__.ragāmum: to claim, to call out a claim: irgumu (ir-gu-mu, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(whatever) he claimed” · iraggum (i-ra-ag-gu-um) “he shall claim” (present with the ventive -m): ul iraggum “he shall not claim” · iraggumū (i-ra-ag-gu-mu) “they shall lay claim” (present plural, no ventive): ana wardūtim ul iraggumū “they shall not lay claim for slavery”
__broaden__.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be put”: ul iššakkan “it shall not be put (in the account)” · to set, put, impose: ištakan (iš-ta-ka-an, perfect, “has set”), išakkan (present) — išakkanšima (i-ša-ak-ka-an-ši-ma, with -ši and -ma) “he/she shall set (it) on her, and”, as in abbuttam išakkan · išakkanūši “they shall set (her on a stake)”, išakkanūšumma “they shall set (it) aside for him, and” · idiom panam šakānum (panam ištakan) “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind · iššakkan also written iš-ta-ak-ka-an (Harper’s reading, UNCERTAIN): andurār amtim iššakkan “the release of the slave-woman shall be established”
__broaden__.leqûm: to take: ileqqi “he shall take” · ilqi “he took” (il-qi₂), ilqû (subjunctive, il-qu₂-u₂), ilqēma (il-qi₂-e-ma) “he took, and”, ilteqēma (perfect, il-te-qi₂-ma) “he has taken, and”; ša … ilqû “which he took” · ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took, and” (preterite ilqe + -ma, here without a spelled e); ilteqe (il-te-qi₂, perfect) “he has taken”; ileqqi (i-li-qi₂, present) “he shall take”; leqîm (li-qi₂-im, infinitive, genitive): ina kaspim leqîm “in the taking of the silver” · ileqqûma (i-li-qu₂-ma) “they shall take, and” (present plural + -ma); ileqqēma “he shall take, and” · ileqqû (i-li-qu₂-u) “they shall take” (present plural, without -ma)
__broaden__.maḫrûm: first, former, previous: maḫrītim in šattim maḫrītim “in the previous year” · maḫru (maḫ-ru) “first, foremost” (an adjective or a stative of maḫārum): ša īnšu maḫru, read “the son he favours” (UNCERTAIN) · maḫrūtum (maḫ-ru-tum, plural in -ūtum) “the former ones”, said of children, in contrast to warkûm “later”
__broaden__.mutum: husband (short u; Harper “husband”; mūtum “death” is another word, spelled the same, so the sense rests on context): mutiša “her husband”, mussa “her husband” (written mu-za, -ša after the t), mut “husband of” (construct; mut libbiša “the husband of her heart”) · mutiša panîm / warkîm “her former / later husband”, with mutiša followed by an adjective in the genitive
